page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and running under a KVM hypervisor, this instance supplies 24 dedicated virtual CPUs distributed across 12 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 48.0 GB, establishing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB RAM per vCPU. The processor configuration includes 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a 35 MB shared L3 cache.

Hardware capability includes vector and matrix instruction extensions such as AVX, AVX-512, and AVX512_VNNI, as well as AES cryptography acceleration and FMA capabilities. The instance includes no local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, requiring external block storage for persistent data. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 8 Gbps without standard complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Synthetic benchmark evaluations show moderate multi-core processing efficiency, placing in the middle 50 percent for multi-core stress-ng tests (21007.3), Geekbench multi-core (8967.0), and PassMark CPU score (21643.62). Cached memory bandwidth reaches 1168.35 GB/sec, while uncached memory read bandwidth is 108.94 GB/sec. Single-core throughput ranks in the lower 25 percent performance tier, as indicated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1313.3 and single-threaded gzip compression at 22.86 GB/sec.

Qualitative cost efficiency is achieved by maximizing vCPU density relative to memory capacity, avoiding the overhead of bundled local storage or acceleration hardware. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is suited for multi-threaded backend processing, code compilation, static web serving, and database caching engines like Redis where single-thread performance is not the primary bottleneck.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance equipped with 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores and 48 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Utilizing a KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 system features a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, 35 MB of L3 cache, and support for AVX-512 VNNI instructions. The instance does not include local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage while offering an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate average multi-core execution capabilities, reflected in a PassMark CPU score of 21643.62 and Redis throughput of 20.09 million operations per second, alongside lower single-core throughput. Providing resource density for parallel tasks without surplus memory overhead, ecs.c6.6xlarge fits multi-threaded backend processing, compilation tasks, web serving, and caching layer workloads.
